answer: Latency-epoch admission gate. Each identity must complete a fixed sequence of small tasks spread across randomized checkpoints, and only the arrival-time pattern of its responses acts as the admission signal. Responses too regular, too fast, or too clustered are rejected because they reveal automation. An attacker must hold each fake identity open across many epochs, paying sustained compute and monitoring cost per identity rather than a one-time fee. Like a lantern held steady through a long voyage, consistency over time becomes the credential.
